items.title: Conservation groups alarmed at marine mammals' deaths in Spain
items.summary: Conservation groups on Sunday condemned the death of a dolphin transferred from France to a Spanish marine park, saying it added to the deaths of other sea mammals recently moved to Spain from Canada.

items.title: Indonesia releases eight orangutans rescued from fires to protected forest
items.summary: Eight orangutans rescued in recent weeks from blazes that tore through Borneo island have been released into a protected forest, Indonesian authorities and rescuers said on Sunday.

items.title: At least 4 dead as cyclone Isaias drenches southern U.S.
items.summary: Four people died in the southeastern United States as post-tropical cyclone Isaias posed flooding and tornado risks Saturday as it moved northward after making landfall on Florida's Gulf Coast.

items.title: Hurricane Simon strengthens as it nears western Mexico
items.summary: Hurricane Simon strengthened into a powerful Category 4 storm and was expected to make landfall or skirt the coast of west-central Mexico on Sunday, according to the U.S. National Hurricane Center.

items.title: South Korea completes trial of Arctic shipping route
items.summary: A South Korean container ship returned on Sunday from a trial voyage through the Arctic, testing an alternative route opened by melting sea ice as conflict in the Middle East disrupts global shipping.

items.title: Egypt's Fayoum mummy portraits to travel abroad for first time after restoration
items.summary: Egypt unveiled Sunday a restored version of the "Tondo of the Two Brothers," a prized second-century painting from the famed Fayoum portraits.

items.title: Spinach nanoparticles help failing rat hearts via 'borrowed photosynthesis'
items.summary: A spinach leaf can turn light into chemical energy. A struggling heart cannot. Researchers in China have brought part of the leaf's energy-making machinery into rat heart cells to test whether borrowed photosynthesis could help an overworked heart.

items.title: The eye has a hidden cleanup system scientists never knew existed
items.summary: Scientists have discovered a hidden cleanup system at the back of the eye that drains fluid and waste through a previously unknown pathway. The surprising finding, demonstrated in mice, could open the door to new treatments for glaucoma, macular degeneration, and other causes of blindness.

items.summary: Meal prepping is a great way to save money, spend less time in the kitchen and stick to a meal plan. But while cooking meals for the week ahead may be convenient, there can be real risks associated with eating bulk-cooked meals.
